messages.author: 324a48ec0ef49f09
messages.subject: brew+PHP
parts:
Hey guys,

I want to mix rapache and php in the same file. is there a way to do
this?
Basically I would like something that looks like this

<?php
// code
?>

<%
## code
%>


is this possible using brew? I dont need to pass variables back and
forth.
-Chris

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: brew+PHP
parts:
I recommend you to rethink the problem. What do you actually want to do? <?php /* code */ ?> <%# R code %> can mean lots of stuff.
You can send POST request via PHP cURL module to RApache and use output buffering to grab output from R script, hence put it in your PHP code.

for sending POST requests via PHP, see this link: http://davidwalsh.name/execute-http-post-php-curl
for output buffering, see official manual pages: http://www.php.net/manual/en/book.outcontrol.php

You should do something like this:

<?php

ob_start();
// send POST request with PHP
// R echoes some output
$output = ob_get_clean();
// do stuff with $output

?>

It's advisable to serialize R output to JSON (see RJSONIO package, toJSON() method), and decode it in PHP with json_decode(). But... as you like it...

Note that, in this case, you rarely need to use brew. I don't like the whole idea of using brew to shove R code into HTML/PHP pages. I salute latter approach for dynamic reports in LaTeX, but I tend to evaluate R scripts with sys.source.

messages.author: a00cf91cbd7ec133
messages.subject: Re: brew+PHP
parts:
Why not execute R from PHP instead of using the brew method? 
 
Basically, you have your login stuff in the PHP file and then do a "exec" command in PHP to run the R script.   You would output a text file with commands, etc. (that can include variables/data from POST) and then execute R on it.
 
This website has an example of how they did it for their needs.
 
http://www.stanford.edu/~mjockers/cgi-bin/drupal/node/25
 
-jeff

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: brew+PHP
parts:
I don't like $_SESSION vars, since their safety is quite questionable. But, anyway... you can put your R scripts outside web root, or use .htaccess to prevent direct access to scripts. It's pretty much a standard technique to prevent access to include scripts. http://stackoverflow.com/questions/409496/prevent-direct-access-to-a-php-include-file
By doing so, your R scripts cannot get executed outside PHP scripts. So there...
